newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 7.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Daily Variety - February 7.

text.p: The following stories appeared in Friday's Daily Variety:

* A deal presented to the board of Havas on Thursday calls for the company to acquire a stake in French paycabler Canal Plus from utilities giant Compagnie Generale des Eaux, while CGE will become the lead shareholder of Havas.

* MGM Worldwide Television has signed an exclusive, multiyear production and development deal with Trilogy Television worth about $12 million-$15 million. The three-year deal with an additional two-year option calls for Trilogy TV, a new unit of Trilogy Entertainment Group, to develop and produce network series, miniseries and telefilms, in addition to animation and other programming for pay cable and firstrun syndication.

* The kids upfront market wrapped up Thursday after a two-day buying frenzy, with early estimates pegging the networks' take at about $765 million, a 5 percent increase from last year, despite sagging broadcast ratings. Most networks secured unit-rate, or cost-per-thousand, increases in the 18 to 20 percent range, which offset the ratings declines, translating to dollar volume about equal to last year for many.

* The developers of the Playa Vista project have reached an agreement in principle with a new group of partners that will bring in the roughly $200 million needed to move the project forward with DreamWorks as its major tenant. Maguire Thomas Partners said Thursday that it has chosen Pacific Capital Group, led by Beverly Hills financier Gary Winnick, whose team also includes Union Labor Life Insurance Co and the J E Robert Co.

* Promotor Michael Cohl and his the Next Adventure outfit may still be looking for millions in financing needed to launch the U2 concert tour. A proposal circulated by Cohl to investors is offering a 25 percent cut of the tour for $15 million, or for the hearty investor, a $30 million check will buy a piece of the 1997-98 U2 tour and the 1997-98 Rolling Stones tour.

* The "English Patient," "Shine," "Secrets & Lies" and "Fargo" won nominations Thursday for the Writers Guild of America Awards. In television nominations, NBC's "Law & Order" and "Seinfeld" each earned three nominations. NBC is owned by General Electric.

* New rules governing Oscar eligibility for documentaries could make life more difficult for nonfiction filmmakers hoping to qualify for an Academy Award nomination. The Academy of Motion Picture Arts & Sciences Thursday released a revised set of requirements for documentaries released during the 1997 awards year requiring a six-month window between the beginning of a film's one-week Oscar-qualifying theatrical run and any appearance on broadcast or cable television.
